author: Mark Atwood
text:
Closed 2026-05-13 by backport edit.

Inserted 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section into crate-jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md between 'Reference Pattern' and 'Non-Interactive Shell Commands' (same position as chat-server). File grew from 109 to 136 lines.

Shape mirrors the canonical chat-server section verbatim for the first two paragraphs (workspace-wide policy on backend-canonical enforcement + the principal_id seam). Third paragraph is mail-specific:

  * $seen / MailboxRights.maySetSeen on shared Mailboxes (RFC 8621 §2)
  * Mailbox.myRights (RFC 8621 §2)
  * Identity / EmailSubmission ownership (RFC 8621 §6, §7)
  * Closing line: 'the backend's /set impl is the canonical point of enforcement' (matches the calendars/contacts sibling phrasing)

The 'workspace-wide bridge' sentence in the second paragraph was also tuned to mail terms: 'shared-mailbox ACLs or per-user keyword state' replaces chat's 'chat role-hierarchy or per-user visibility scoping'.

Cross-verified against calendars-server and contacts-server: the per-sibling implications paragraphs were already swapped under JMAP-sc1b.109 — the 'Sweep follow-up' note in this bead's original description was outdated. The 6 siblings already carry their own tailored paragraphs; this commit closes out the canonical mail-server to match.
